title: A single tap arrives with no eventType, so === CLICK_EVENT never matches
claim: The handle-input skill says a single press arrives as a sysEvent whose eventType is undefined, because protobuf omits the zero value, and tells apps to compare eventType ?? 0. The Your First App page handles both CLICK_EVENT and undefined.
actual: On simulator 0.9.5 and on G2 hardware, a single tap delivers a sysEvent whose whole payload is { eventSource: 1 }. The eventType key is missing, and CLICK_EVENT is 0, so eventType === OsEventTypeList.CLICK_EVENT is never true. A double tap carries eventType 3 as expected. All four official templates in evenhub-templates coalesced the missing field to null and never fired on a tap, until a merged change on 2026-08-07 made them coalesce to 0 when the envelope is present. The SDK behaviour is unchanged.
impact: Tap handlers that compare against CLICK_EVENT silently never run. Apps scaffolded from the templates before 2026-08-07 still carry the bug.
workaround: Coalesce only when the envelope exists: event.sysEvent ? (event.sysEvent.eventType ?? 0) : null. Coalescing the optional chain (event.sysEvent?.eventType ?? 0) turns every other event into a tap.

evidence.note: Taps were dead in the text-heavy template; the fix was checked in the simulator. Merged 2026-08-07 for all four templates.
Raw host message for a click: {"type":"ListenEvenAppData","method":"evenHubEvent","data":["sysEvent",{"eventSource":1}]}. A double click carries eventType 3.
